item.title: The Numbers Don’t Add Up: Women Continue to Earn Less, Regardless of Occupation - IWPR
item.description: In 2025, women were paid less than men for full-time work in all 20 occupations that employ the most women and in all 20 occupations that employ the most men in the United States. Across all detailed occupations with sufficient data, women were paid up to $846 less per week compared to men in the same occupation. item.title: Filling the Gap: Community College Students Expect Sexual Health Education on Campus - IWPR
item.description: Decades of research point to the importance of comprehensive sex education for promoting health beliefs and behaviors that lead to healthier relationships and reduce young people’s risk for unplanned pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs). But a survey of community college students found that only 15 percent report having received comprehensive sex education. item.title: AANHPI Women’s Equal Pay Day: Fact vs. Fiction About the Wage Gap - IWPR
item.description: In 2024, Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander (AANHPI) women earned approximately 83 cents for every dollar paid to non-Hispanic White men, a widely cited benchmark that offers an important snapshot of overall pay equity. item.title: From 72% to 17%: What Happens When You Stop Outreach to Women for Pre-Apprenticeship Programs - IWPR
item.description: “Women just don’t apply” is a common misunderstanding heard from industry and apprenticeship stakeholders about women’s underrepresentation in the construction trades. Evidence from 12 cohorts (classes) of the co-ed Minuteman “Build It!” Carpentry pre-apprenticeship program in Massachusetts, however, shows that women’s low numbers are far from inevitable, and that their participation dramatically improves with effective [...] The post From 72% to 17%: What Happens When You Stop Outreach to Women

item.title: Numbers Matter: Women Working in Construction in 2025 - IWPR
item.description: In 2025, women construction managers saw a decline in both their employment and their share of jobs. And while women’s share of construction apprentices improved slightly, they remain highly underrepresented. These numbers point to women’s resilience and staying power, but also show uneven progress and continued dramatic underrepresentation in construction. Policymakers and industry leaders [...] The post Numbers Matter: Women Working in Construction in 2025 appeared first on IWPR.

item.title: Unseen Efforts: Disparities in Unpaid Care Work Before and After COVID-19 - IWPR
item.description: The COVID-19 pandemic brought to the fore the need for unpaid care work, as well as the highly unequal distribution of care work. This study contributes to the understanding of care work by providing post-COVID assessments of changes in unpaid caregiving by gender, race/ethnicity, and socioeconomic status.
